problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{18}, & x=0 \\ \frac{2}{9}, & x=1 \\ \frac{1}{2}, & x=2\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{3}].$

feedback.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.25$ | $0.35$ | $0.4$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{4}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{4}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{4}]={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{4}\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{4}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{4}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{4}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={1}^{4}\cdot 0.25+{2}^{4}\cdot 0.35+{3}^{4}\cdot 0.4 \\  & =1\cdot 0.25+16\cdot 0.35+81\cdot 0.4 \\  & =0.25+5.6+32.4 \\  & =38.25.\end{aligned}
$$
